rules.name: Polar question: -aa ending, no kya
rules.l1_habit: Hindi 'क्या' at the start; Telugu marks yes/no questions with -ā on the verb/noun
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: Questions: add -ā at the end, no ‘क्या’
rules.title_hi: हाँ/ना वाले सवाल: आख़िर में -आ (ా), 'क्या' नहीं
rules.explain_hi: Hindi में सवाल 'क्या' से शुरू होता है। Telugu में 'क्या' नहीं लगता — आख़िरी शब्द के अंत में -आ (ా) जुड़ जाता है: వస్తావు (आओगे) → వస్తావా (आओगे?)।

rules.name: Zero copula: no 'is' between two nouns
rules.l1_habit: Hindi है is always present; Telugu leaves it out in 'X is Y'
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: No word for ‘is’ in ‘This is a book’
rules.explain_hi: 'यह किताब है' = ఇది పుస్తకం — बस। ఉంది का मतलब 'मौजूद है/रखा है', 'यह X है' कहने के लिए नहीं।

rules.name: Possession with dative: 'to me is a book'
rules.l1_habit: Hindi मेरे पास / मुझे; learner uses nominative 'I' + ఉంది
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: ‘I have’ is ‘to me there is’ (నాకు … ఉంది)
rules.explain_hi: Telugu में 'मेरे पास किताब है' ऐसे कहते हैं: 'मुझको (నాకు) एक किताब है (ఉంది)'। नेनु (నేను = मैं) नहीं, नाकु (నాకు = मुझको)।

rules.name: Case endings attach to the noun (no separate 'in')
rules.l1_habit: Hindi में is a separate word; Telugu -lō is a suffix and the noun changes (ఇల్లు→ఇంట్లో)
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: ‘in’ sticks to the word (ఇంట్లో = in the house)
rules.title_hi: 'में' शब्द से चिपकता है: ఇంట్లో = घर में
rules.explain_hi: 'घर में' = ఇల్లు + లో → ఇంట్లో (एक ही शब्द)। -లో (में) अलग शब्द नहीं, शब्द के साथ जुड़ता है।

rules.name: Negation: negative verb form, not 'not' after verb
rules.l1_habit: Hindi नहीं before the verb; Telugu uses a negative verb form (రాను) or కాదు only for nouns
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: Saying ‘not’: change the verb (రాను = I won't come)
rules.title_hi: 'नहीं' के लिए verb ही बदलता है: రాను = नहीं आऊँगा
rules.explain_hi: Hindi में 'नहीं' अलग शब्द है। Telugu में verb का रूप ही बदल जाता है: వస్తాను (आऊँगा) → రాను (नहीं आऊँगा)। కాదు (नहीं है) यहाँ नहीं लगता।

rules.name: 'We': మేము (without you) vs మనం (with you)
rules.l1_habit: Hindi has one हम; Telugu splits inclusive and exclusive
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review

items.hindi: हम (तुम और मैं) जा रहे हैं।

rules.title: Two words for ‘we’: మేము and మనం
rules.title_hi: 'हम' के दो शब्द: మేము और మనం
rules.explain_hi: మేము = हम (सुनने वाला शामिल नहीं)। మనం = हम (तुम भी शामिल)। 'हम तुम्हारे बिना जा रहे हैं' → మేము; 'तुम और मैं जा रहे हैं' → మనం।

rules.name: 'He' vs 'she' pronouns (Hindi वह is gender-neutral)
rules.l1_habit: Hindi वह covers he and she; Telugu uses అతను / ఆమె
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: ‘He’ and ‘she’ are different words
rules.title_hi: 'वह' के दो शब्द: అతను (आदमी) और ఆమె (औरत)
rules.explain_hi: Hindi का 'वह' आदमी और औरत दोनों के लिए है। Telugu में आदमी के लिए అతను, औरत के लिए ఆమె।

rules.name: Third-person verb ending follows he / she (positive-transfer control)
rules.l1_habit: Hindi verbs also agree in gender, so this is expected to be easy; used as a control
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: Verb endings for ‘he’ and ‘she’
rules.title_hi: verb का अंत भी 'वह' के हिसाब से: వస్తాడు / వస్తుంది
rules.explain_hi: जैसे Hindi में 'आता/आती', वैसे Telugu में आदमी के लिए వస్తాడు और औरत के लिए వస్తుంది।

rules.name: Respect: మీరు takes the plural -āru ending
rules.l1_habit: Hindi आप takes plural verb; learner keeps singular -āvu/-āvā after మీరు
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: Respect: మీరు takes a plural ending
rules.title_hi: आदर: మీరు (आप) के साथ verb भी आदर वाला
rules.explain_hi: 'आप' = మీరు, और verb भी आदर वाले रूप में: వస్తారా (आ रहे हैं?), తింటారు (खाते हैं) — వస్తావా/తింటావు 'तुम' के लिए है।

rules.name: Relative clause: participle before the noun, no 'jo'
rules.l1_habit: Hindi जो…वह clause after/before; Telugu uses a -ina participle before the noun
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review

items.english: This is the book that I read.
items.hindi: यह वह किताब है जो मैंने पढ़ी।

rules.title: ‘The book I read’: the describing part comes first
rules.title_hi: 'जो मैंने पढ़ी वो किताब': बताने वाला हिस्सा पहले
rules.explain_hi: Telugu में 'जो' नहीं होता। 'मेरी पढ़ी हुई किताब' जैसा कहते हैं: నేను చదివిన పుస్తకం — बताने वाला हिस्सा संज्ञा (किताब) से पहले।

rules.name: No 'ne' marking: subject stays in the plain form in the past
rules.l1_habit: Hindi ने on past transitive subject; learner marks Telugu subject with a case ending
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: No ‘ने’ in Telugu
rules.explain_hi: 'उसने किताब पढ़ी' = అతను పుస్తకం చదివాడు। कर्ता (మైం/वह) वैसा ही रहता है: నేను, అతను — నాకు/అతనికి ('मुझको/उसको') नहीं।

rules.name: Object with -ను when it is a person
rules.l1_habit: Hindi को is optional-ish; learner drops Telugu -ను on animate objects
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: Add -ను when the object is a person
rules.explain_hi: 'माँ को बुलाया' = అమ్మను పిలిచాను। जब काम किसी इंसान पर हो, तो उसके नाम के साथ -ను (को) जुड़ता है।

rules.name: Present continuous: -tunnānu, not verb + 'am'
rules.l1_habit: Hindi रहा हूँ is two words; Telugu fuses it, or uses -tū unnānu
rules.source: Claude draft (unreviewed) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: ‘I am coming’ is one word: వస్తున్నాను
rules.explain_hi: 'खा रहा हूँ' = తింటున్నాను (एक ही शब्द)। తింటాను (खाऊँगा) + ఉన్నాను (हूँ) अलग-अलग नहीं जोड़ते।

rules.name: 'For': కోసం comes after the noun
rules.l1_habit: Hindi के लिए follows the noun, but learner puts కోసం first like an English preposition
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: ‘For’: కోసం comes after the word
rules.explain_hi: 'तुम्हारे लिए' = నీ కోసం। जैसे Hindi में 'लिए' बाद में आता है, Telugu में भी కోసం बाद में आता है।

rules.name: Going to a place: -కి, not -లో
rules.source: Claude draft; contrast confirmed in Krishnamurti & Gwynn 1985 examples (see book_examples.jsonl) · team rule bank (FavianaNoronha/LMA---Reverse-learning-Tutor) · Hindi explanations drafted by Claude (AI), need review
rules.title: Going somewhere: use -కి, not -లో
rules.explain_hi: 'घर जा रहा हूँ' = ఇంటికి వెళ్తున్నాను। जगह की तरफ़ जाने के लिए -కి (को/की तरफ़); -లో का मतलब 'के अंदर'।
